en.greeting: Hi! Today we learn sentences with if: things that are always true, things that may happen in the future, and when to say when instead. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Always true: if + present
steps.text: Let's start with sentences about things that happen **every time**.
steps.body: A sentence with **if** has two parts: the **if-part** (the condition: *If you heat ice*) and the **result** (*it melts*). When the result happens **every time** (a fact or a habit), use the **present simple** in both parts. This is the **zero conditional**. **No will**: not 'it will melts'. And add **-s** after he/she/it in both parts: *If Budi eats chilli, he gets a stomachache.*

pairs.en: If you heat ice, it melts.
pairs.id: Kalau es dipanaskan, es itu meleleh.

pairs.en: If you don't water plants, they die.
pairs.id: Kalau tanaman tidak disiram, tanaman itu mati.

pairs.en: If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep.
pairs.id: Kalau saya minum kopi malam-malam, saya tidak bisa tidur.

pairs.en: If Budi eats chilli, he gets a stomachache.
pairs.id: Kalau Budi makan cabai, perutnya sakit.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: A science fact: it's true every time.

question.prompt: Complete: If you heat water to 100°C, it ___.
question.explanation: Water boils at 100°C **every time**, so use the present simple: **it boils**, with **-s** for *it*. 'boil' has no -s, and 'will boils' is wrong twice: a fact needs no will, and there's never -s after will.

steps.title: One possible future: if + present, will
steps.text: Now a different situation: **one time in the future** that **may** happen.
steps.body: Maybe it rains tomorrow, maybe not. If it does, here's the result: *If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.* Use **if + present simple, will / won't + verb**: the **first conditional**. Ask yourself: **every time** (fact, habit) → present, present. **One time, later** (tomorrow, tonight, this weekend) → present, **will**. Indonesian trap: *Kalau besok hujan, saya di rumah saja* has no *akan*, but English needs **will** in the result.

pairs.en: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
pairs.id: Kalau besok hujan, saya di rumah saja.

pairs.en: If you hurry, you'll catch the bus.
pairs.id: Kalau kamu cepat, kamu akan dapat busnya.

pairs.en: If the traffic is bad, we'll be late.
pairs.id: Kalau macet, kita akan terlambat.

pairs.en: If Rina is tired tonight, she won't cook.
pairs.id: Kalau nanti malam Rina capek, dia tidak akan masak.

steps.title: No will after if
steps.text: The if-part talks about the future, but it has **no will**. Look at the verb after **if** in each sentence.
steps.body: Not 'If it will rain'. The word **if** already shows we're imagining the future, so the verb after it stays **present**. Indonesian adds *nanti* or *akan* (*Kalau nanti hujan …*), English doesn't: just **If it rains** (you can add *tomorrow*). **will** goes only in the result. And keep the **-s**: *If Rina comes*, not 'If Rina come'.

examples.en: If it rains, I'll stay home.
examples.id: Kalau nanti hujan, saya di rumah saja.

examples.en: If Rina comes tonight, we'll eat together.
examples.id: Kalau nanti malam Rina datang, kita makan bersama.

examples.en: If the shop is open, I'll buy some bread.
examples.id: Kalau tokonya buka, saya akan beli roti.

examples.en: If you need help, I'll be in my room.
examples.id: Kalau kamu butuh bantuan, saya ada di kamar.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina has a job interview in Jakarta tomorrow.

question.prompt: Complete: If she ___ the job, she'll move to Jakarta.
question.explanation: No will in the if-part, even about the future: **If she gets the job**. *she* needs **-s**, so 'get' is wrong. **will** goes in the result: *she'll move*.

steps.title: Two orders and the comma
steps.text: You can swap the two parts. Only the comma changes.
steps.body: **if-part first** → put a **comma** after it: *If you're hungry, I'll make some noodles.* **Result first** → **no comma**: *I'll make some noodles if you're hungry.* The meaning is the same. When you speak, the comma is a short pause. It works the same for facts (*If you heat ice, it melts.*) and for **when**.

pairs.en: If you're hungry, I'll make some noodles.
pairs.id: Kalau kamu lapar, saya buatkan mi.

pairs.en: I'll make some noodles if you're hungry.
pairs.id: Saya buatkan mi kalau kamu lapar.

pairs.en: If Budi calls, I'll tell you.
pairs.id: Kalau Budi menelepon, saya kasih tahu kamu.

pairs.en: I'll tell you if Budi calls.
pairs.id: Saya kasih tahu kamu kalau Budi menelepon.

steps.title: Where's the comma?
steps.text: One of these sentences is missing a comma.

question.explanation: In **If you're tired I'll drive**, the if-part comes first, so it needs a comma: **If you're tired, I'll drive.** In *I'll drive if you're tired*, the result comes first, so no comma.

steps.title: if (maybe) or when (sure)?
steps.text: Indonesian **kalau** can mean **if** or **when**. English makes you choose.
steps.body: **if** = **maybe**: you're not sure it will happen. *If I see Budi, I'll tell him.* **when** = **sure**: it will happen, just later. *When I get home, I'll call you.* So 'If I get home tonight, I'll call you' sounds like you may not get home! After **when**, the same rule: present, **no will** (*When I get home*, not 'When I will get home'). For facts, if and when mean almost the same (*When you heat ice, it melts*): a fact is always sure.

pairs.en: If I see Budi, I'll tell him.
pairs.id: Kalau saya ketemu Budi, saya akan bilang ke dia. (mungkin)

pairs.en: When I get home, I'll call you.
pairs.id: Nanti kalau sudah sampai rumah, saya telepon kamu. (pasti)

pairs.en: If it's sunny on Sunday, we'll go to the park.
pairs.id: Kalau hari Minggu cerah, kita akan ke taman. (mungkin)

pairs.en: When the class finishes, I'll eat lunch.
pairs.id: Nanti kalau kelasnya selesai, saya makan siang. (pasti)

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Budi is on the train to Bandung. It arrives at 4 p.m. He sends a message to his mum.

question.prompt: Complete: '___, I'll send you a photo of the station.'
question.explanation: Budi is sure he'll arrive, so use **when**, with the present: **When I arrive**. 'If I arrive' sounds like he may never get there, and there's no will after when.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: It's raining hard. The rain is sure to stop later.

question.prompt: Arrange the words, starting with When: Nanti kalau hujannya sudah berhenti, kita pulang.
question.solution: When the rain stops, we'll go home.
question.explanation: The rain is **sure** to stop, so **When**. After when, the present: **the rain stops** (+s, no will). The when-part comes first, so a comma, then **we'll go home**.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita belajar kalimat dengan if: hal yang selalu benar, hal yang mungkin terjadi nanti, dan kapan memakai when. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Selalu benar: if + present
steps.text: Kita mulai dengan kalimat tentang hal yang terjadi **setiap kali**.
steps.body: Kalimat dengan **if** (kalau) punya dua bagian: **bagian if** (syaratnya: *If you heat ice*) dan **hasilnya** (*it melts*). Kalau hasilnya terjadi **setiap kali** (fakta atau kebiasaan), pakai **present simple** di kedua bagian. Ini namanya **zero conditional**. **Tanpa will**: bukan 'it will melts'. Dan tambahkan **-s** setelah he/she/it di kedua bagian: *If Budi eats chilli, he gets a stomachache.*

pairs.en: If you heat ice, it melts.
pairs.id: Kalau es dipanaskan, es itu meleleh.

pairs.en: If you don't water plants, they die.
pairs.id: Kalau tanaman tidak disiram, tanaman itu mati.

pairs.en: If I drink coffee at night, I can't sleep.
pairs.id: Kalau saya minum kopi malam-malam, saya tidak bisa tidur.

pairs.en: If Budi eats chilli, he gets a stomachache.
pairs.id: Kalau Budi makan cabai, perutnya sakit.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Fakta ilmiah: selalu benar setiap kali.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: If you heat water to 100°C, it ___.
question.explanation: Air mendidih pada 100°C **setiap kali**, jadi pakai present simple: **it boils**, dengan **-s** untuk *it*. 'boil' tidak memakai -s, dan 'will boils' salah dua kali: fakta tidak butuh will, dan tidak pernah ada -s setelah will.

steps.title: Satu kemungkinan nanti: if + present, will
steps.text: Sekarang situasi yang lain: **satu kali di masa depan** yang **mungkin** terjadi.
steps.body: Mungkin besok hujan, mungkin tidak. Kalau hujan, inilah hasilnya: *If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.* Pakai **if + present simple, will / won't + kata kerja**: ini **first conditional**. Tanyakan: **setiap kali** (fakta, kebiasaan) → present, present. **Satu kali, nanti** (besok, nanti malam, akhir pekan ini) → present, **will**. Jebakan bahasa Indonesia: *Kalau besok hujan, saya di rumah saja* tidak memakai *akan*, tapi bahasa Inggris butuh **will** di bagian hasil.

pairs.en: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay home.
pairs.id: Kalau besok hujan, saya di rumah saja.

pairs.en: If you hurry, you'll catch the bus.
pairs.id: Kalau kamu cepat, kamu akan dapat busnya.

pairs.en: If the traffic is bad, we'll be late.
pairs.id: Kalau macet, kita akan terlambat.

pairs.en: If Rina is tired tonight, she won't cook.
pairs.id: Kalau nanti malam Rina capek, dia tidak akan masak.

steps.title: Tanpa will setelah if
steps.text: Bagian if membicarakan masa depan, tapi **tanpa will**. Perhatikan kata kerja setelah **if** di setiap kalimat.
steps.body: Bukan 'If it will rain'. Kata **if** sudah menunjukkan kita sedang membayangkan masa depan, jadi kata kerja setelahnya tetap **present**. Bahasa Indonesia menambah *nanti* atau *akan* (*Kalau nanti hujan …*), bahasa Inggris tidak: cukup **If it rains** (boleh ditambah *tomorrow*). **will** hanya ada di bagian hasil. Dan jangan lupa **-s**: *If Rina comes*, bukan 'If Rina come'.

examples.en: If it rains, I'll stay home.
examples.id: Kalau nanti hujan, saya di rumah saja.

examples.en: If Rina comes tonight, we'll eat together.
examples.id: Kalau nanti malam Rina datang, kita makan bersama.

examples.en: If the shop is open, I'll buy some bread.
examples.id: Kalau tokonya buka, saya akan beli roti.

examples.en: If you need help, I'll be in my room.
examples.id: Kalau kamu butuh bantuan, saya ada di kamar.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Besok Rina wawancara kerja di Jakarta.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: If she ___ the job, she'll move to Jakarta.
question.explanation: Tidak ada will di bagian if, walaupun tentang masa depan: **If she gets the job**. *she* butuh **-s**, jadi 'get' salah. **will** ada di bagian hasil: *she'll move*.

steps.title: Dua urutan dan koma
steps.text: Kedua bagian boleh ditukar. Yang berubah hanya komanya.
steps.body: **Bagian if di depan** → beri **koma** setelahnya: *If you're hungry, I'll make some noodles.* **Hasil di depan** → **tanpa koma**: *I'll make some noodles if you're hungry.* Artinya sama. Saat bicara, koma itu jeda pendek. Aturan ini sama untuk fakta (*If you heat ice, it melts.*) dan untuk **when**.

pairs.en: If you're hungry, I'll make some noodles.
pairs.id: Kalau kamu lapar, saya buatkan mi.

pairs.en: I'll make some noodles if you're hungry.
pairs.id: Saya buatkan mi kalau kamu lapar.

pairs.en: If Budi calls, I'll tell you.
pairs.id: Kalau Budi menelepon, saya kasih tahu kamu.

pairs.en: I'll tell you if Budi calls.
pairs.id: Saya kasih tahu kamu kalau Budi menelepon.

steps.title: Di mana komanya?
steps.text: Salah satu kalimat ini kurang koma.

question.explanation: Di **If you're tired I'll drive**, bagian if ada di depan, jadi butuh koma: **If you're tired, I'll drive.** Di *I'll drive if you're tired*, hasilnya di depan, jadi tanpa koma.

steps.title: if (mungkin) atau when (pasti)?
steps.text: Kata **kalau** bisa berarti **if** atau **when**. Bahasa Inggris membuatmu memilih.
steps.body: **if** = **mungkin**: kamu belum yakin itu akan terjadi. *If I see Budi, I'll tell him.* **when** = **pasti**: itu akan terjadi, hanya nanti. *When I get home, I'll call you.* Jadi 'If I get home tonight, I'll call you' terdengar seolah kamu mungkin tidak sampai rumah! Setelah **when**, aturannya sama: present, **tanpa will** (*When I get home*, bukan 'When I will get home'). Untuk fakta, if dan when artinya hampir sama (*When you heat ice, it melts*): fakta selalu pasti.

pairs.en: If I see Budi, I'll tell him.
pairs.id: Kalau saya ketemu Budi, saya akan bilang ke dia. (mungkin)

pairs.en: When I get home, I'll call you.
pairs.id: Nanti kalau sudah sampai rumah, saya telepon kamu. (pasti)

pairs.en: If it's sunny on Sunday, we'll go to the park.
pairs.id: Kalau hari Minggu cerah, kita akan ke taman. (mungkin)

pairs.en: When the class finishes, I'll eat lunch.
pairs.id: Nanti kalau kelasnya selesai, saya makan siang. (pasti)

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Budi sedang di kereta ke Bandung. Keretanya tiba jam 4 sore. Dia mengirim pesan ke ibunya.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: '___, I'll send you a photo of the station.'
question.explanation: Budi pasti akan tiba, jadi pakai **when**, dengan present: **When I arrive**. 'If I arrive' terdengar seolah dia mungkin tidak pernah sampai, dan tidak ada will setelah when.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Hujan deras. Hujannya pasti berhenti nanti.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya, mulai dengan When: Nanti kalau hujannya sudah berhenti, kita pulang.
question.solution: When the rain stops, we'll go home.
question.explanation: Hujannya **pasti** berhenti, jadi **When**. Setelah when, pakai present: **the rain stops** (+s, tanpa will). Bagian when ada di depan, jadi pakai koma, lalu **we'll go home**.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semuanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.
